US Liquidity and Monetary Conditions
Synthesises Federal Reserve liquidity measures, money supply, real-rate signals and SOFR positioning to assess the current US monetary and liquidity regime.

Regime Assessment:

  • Regime: Transitional / Fragile Balance
  • Regime Confidence Index: Medium Confidence
  • Status: The regime is fragile.

Why This Regime:

  • Stabilization of Federal Reserve assets and falling reverse repo usage provide a neutral liquidity base (1).
  • Medium-term expectations are shifting toward easing as evidenced by long-biased build in 5-year SOFR markets (5).
  • Dynamic weighting favored signals with high interpretation confidence and structural relevance, such as the Liquidity Composite (1).
  • The Real Interest Rate Trend was downweighted due to internal conflict and low conviction (3).
  • M2 Money Supply was downweighted because momentum gains conflict with low year-over-year growth levels (2).

Alignment & Tensions:

  • Liquidity stabilization aligns with positive 3-month M2 momentum (1)(2).
  • Tactical tension exists between extreme short positioning in front-end SOFR and long-biased builds in 5-year SOFR (4)(5).
  • Tensions do not overturn the regime because cyclical liquidity trends are outweighing tactical positioning extremes (1).

Scenario Balance:

  • Dominant scenario: Persistence in a neutral state as balance sheet contraction ceases (1).
  • Primary upside risk: Accelerated M2 growth removes internal conflict and confirms expansion (2).
  • Primary downside risk: Re-acceleration of real rates driven by hawkish policy repricing (3).

What Would Change the Regime:

  • A reversal in reverse repo usage or a return to negative Fed asset growth (1).
  • A drop in 3-month M2 momentum below -1.0% signaling a liquidity withdrawal (2).
  • Real yields falling more than 0.05% below the 6-month moving average (3).

Model Lineage

Visualisations below present upstream signal states and evidence context used to form the current silver market interpretation.

Federal Reserve Liquidity Composite Signal

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given the positive inflection in FED_Signal assets and sustained Bullish RRP_Signal usage, this setup aligns with Range-biased price paths and Normal volatility, where the dominant risk is Regime shift, not mean reversion. (1)
  • The signal remains in a Neutral regime as the composite score of 0.17 sits between the defined expansion/contraction thresholds. (1)
  • Conviction Band: Medium; Interpretation Confidence: High Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Improving; Threshold Proximity: Moderate; Revision Sensitivity: Moderate.

Methodology Applied:

  • Liquidity Composite (LC) scores between -0.75 and 0.75 define a Neutral regime where market-neutral or trend-following logic applies. (1)
  • Falling Overnight Reverse Repo (RRP) usage is interpreted as an "inverted signal" indicating incremental easing. (1)
  • Rising composite values indicate expansionary liquidity and inflationary support, while falling values suggest tightening. (1)
  • Federal Reserve Liquidity Composite (latest: 2026-05-31). (1)

Key Dynamics:

  • The primary driver is the stabilization of Federal Reserve Total Assets (YoY), which turned positive (0.83%) for the first time in this cycle. (1)
  • Momentum is positive, with the LC rising from -0.20 to +0.17 over the last 14 months, indicating a steady drainage of contractionary pressure. (1)
  • Internal Tension: M2 growth has decelerated slightly from 4.69% to 3.90%, acting as a minor drag on the accelerating Fed balance sheet components. (1)
  • Conditional Invalidation: A reversal in RRP usage (rising usage) or a return to negative Fed asset growth. (1)

Scenario Balance:

  • Dominant base case: Persistence in the Neutral regime with a gradual drift toward Expansionary conditions as balance sheet contraction ceases.
  • Upside risk: Rapid RRP depletion or accelerated M2 growth triggers an early shift to the Expansion regime (LC > 0.75).
  • Downside risk: Renewed balance sheet drainage or a spike in RRP usage returns the signal to a negative trajectory.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months), reflecting the slow-moving nature of monetary aggregates and Fed policy shifts. (1)
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Medium, as the signal is currently in a non-extreme (Neutral) state but showing a clear directional trend.

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs aggregate liquidity availability by measuring the net expansion of central bank and banking system balance sheets. (1)
  • Economic mechanism: The signal tracks the drainage of cash from the Fed's RRP facility back into the financial system, easing short-term funding. (1)
  • Cycle position: Not determined.
  • Interacts with real yields and credit spreads to determine if nominal liquidity growth is translating into lower real funding costs. (1)

Regime Context:

  • Persistent Neutral regime (duration: 35+ months) currently showing a strengthening trend. (1)
  • Direction of change: Strengthening toward the Expansionary threshold.

Model Limitations:

  • Weekly balance sheet data revisions may mask intra-month volatility. (1)
  • Equal weighting assumes constant information value across M2, Fed assets, and reserves. (1)

Data & References:

  • Latest observation: 2026-05-31. (1)
  • Most influential: FED_YoY (0.828%) and RRP_YoY (-97.7%). (1)
  • Public datasets: 10-Year Real Yields and VIX Index would enhance cross-regime validation.
M2 Money Supply Signal

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement (mandatory): Given the M2SL_YoY at 4.57% and M2SL_3Month_Change at 1.48% (1), this setup aligns with Upward-biased price paths and Normal volatility, where the dominant risk is Trend continuation, not Mean reversion.
  • The signal reflects a transition into a Bullish regime, though current values suggest an internal discrepancy with the defined thresholds (1).
  • Conviction Band: Medium, Interpretation Confidence: Mixed Signals, and Internal Conflict Flag: Yes. Signal Stability Assessment: Improving, Threshold Proximity: Near, and Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • Bullish regime requires YoY growth > 6.0% AND 3M momentum > 1.0% (1).
  • Worst-of logic: The signal is downgraded if either the YoY level or 3M momentum falls into a lower tier (1).
  • Bearish regime is triggered if YoY < 2.0% or 3M momentum < -1.0% (1).
  • M2 Money Supply Signal (Latest observation: 2026-03-01) (1).

Key Dynamics:

  • The 3M momentum of 1.48% provides the primary bullish impulse by exceeding the 1.0% threshold (1).
  • Internal Conflict: YoY growth at 4.57% remains below the 6.0% bullish requirement, implying a "Neutral" state under worst-of logic despite the table's label (1).
  • Momentum has stabilized above the 1% threshold for five consecutive months (1).
  • Conditional Invalidation: A drop in 3M momentum below -1.0% or YoY growth below 2.0% (1).

Scenario Balance:

  • Base case dominant: Expansionary liquidity environment supports risk assets as 3M momentum holds positive gains (1).
  • Upside risk: M2 YoY growth accelerates above 6.0%, removing internal conflict and confirming full bullish expansion (1).
  • Downside risk: A sharp contraction in 3M momentum below -1.0% signals a liquidity withdrawal regime shift (1).

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months) as M2 growth trends typically guide medium-term economic expansion (1).
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Medium due to the conflict between categorical labels and the underlying metric thresholds.

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs the liquidity dimension of the macro environment (1).
  • Economic mechanism: Measures supply of liquid assets available for spending; rising growth implies an inflationary and risk-on bias (1).
  • Cycle position: Not determined.
  • Interacts with Fed balance sheet trends and credit creation to assess broad monetary availability (1).

Regime Context:

  • Regime is newly entered as a Bullish label following a transition from Neutral in early 2026 (1).
  • Direction of change: Strengthening momentum within the liquidity supply component.

Model Limitations:

  • M2 does not account for the velocity of money (1).
  • Correlation with CPI varies significantly over different macro horizons (1).

Data & References:

  • M2SL Series Data through 2026-03-01 (1).
  • Data timeliness cannot be assessed.
  • Public datasets for improvement: Fed Balance Sheet (H.4.1) and Consumer Price Index.
Real Interest Rate Trend Signal

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given a real yield of 1.91% and a narrowing 0.02% spread over its 1.89% trend, this setup aligns with Downward-biased price paths and Indeterminate volatility, where the dominant risk is Regime shift, not Mean reversion.
  • The signal is currently in a persistent Bearish regime, though recent data indicates a transition toward a Neutral state (1).
  • Conviction Band: Low; Interpretation Confidence: Mixed Signals; Internal Conflict Flag: Yes. Signal Stability Assessment: Deteriorating; Threshold Proximity: Near; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • Real yield > 0.05% above its 6-month moving average (MA) is classified as Bearish (restrictive) (1).
  • Real yield within +/- 0.05% of its 6-month MA is classified as Neutral (1).
  • Falling values relative to trend imply expansionary regimes; rising values imply tightening or slowdown regimes (1).
  • Dataset: Real Interest Rate Trend Signal, latest observation 2026-05-01 (1).

Key Dynamics:

  • The primary driver is the 10-year TIPS real yield (1.91%), which maintains a positive spread against the 6-month trend (1.89%) (1).
  • Stabilisation is evident as the yield-to-trend divergence narrowed from +0.15% in April to +0.02% in May.
  • Internal Conflict: The provided content labels May as "Bearish" despite the spread falling within the defined 0.05% "Neutral" buffer.
  • Conditional Invalidation: A decline in the 10-year real yield to more than 0.05% below the moving average (1).
  • Signal stability is deteriorating as the restrictive impulse loses momentum.

Scenario Balance:

  • Base case dominant: Continued restrictive pressure as yields remain nominally above the trend line.
  • Most plausible upside risk: Shift to Neutral or Bullish regime triggered by real yields falling below 1.84%.
  • Most plausible downside risk: Re-acceleration of real rates driven by hawkish monetary policy repricing.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months) due to the use of a six-month moving average window (1).
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Medium; the signal effectively identifies shifts in marginal borrowing costs.

Macro Relevance:

  • Macro dimension: Monetary conditions and financial liquidity.
  • Mechanism: Rising real rates increase the cost of capital, creating headwinds for risk assets and economic expansion (1).
  • Cycle position: Transitioning from a restrictive stage toward stabilization (not fully determined).
  • Interacts with nominal yields and breakeven inflation to distinguish between growth and policy drivers (1).

Regime Context:

  • The Bearish regime has been persistent since November 2025.
  • Direction of change: Weakening (moving from strongly restrictive toward a Neutral stance).

Model Limitations:

  • Lagging behavior is inherent due to the moving average window (1).
  • TIPS market liquidity distortions can cause false regime flips during high volatility (1).

Data & References:

  • 10-year TIPS real yield (Value_DFII10), observation date 2026-05-01 (1).
  • Most influential: The 1.91% yield level vs. the 1.888% MA6 trend value (1).
  • 5-year vs 10-year real yield spreads would improve differentiation between policy and growth expectations (1).
SOF 3M - Individual Market Analysis

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given Spec_Net_%OI of -8.6% and a Spec_zscore of -1.94, this setup aligns with Downward-biased price paths and Elevated volatility, where the dominant risk is Mean reversion, not Trend continuation.
  • The signal identifies a "Balanced Short Bias" regime characterized by "High Tension" as positioning approaches tail-risk extremes (1).
  • Conviction Band: Low; Interpretation Confidence: Mixed Signals; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Volatile; Threshold Proximity: Near; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • Positioning Z-scores >= 2 or <= -2 define high tail-risk regimes where trend additions should be avoided in favor of reversal setups (1).
  • Rising short speculative positioning serves as a proxy for a tightening or restrictive monetary policy bias (1).
  • High Tension Scores indicate fragility in the prevailing consensus and increased potential for volatility (1).
  • SOFR-3M Individual Market Analysis (2026-05-12).

Key Dynamics:

  • Speculative stretch is currently at -1.94 standard deviations, placing the market near the "Extreme Crowding" threshold (1).
  • Negative capital flow (-3.5%) aligns with the net short bias, suggesting a "Long Reduction" momentum in recent weeks (1).
  • Hedger positioning is in a "Deep Long" regime (Z-score 1.97), creating structural mean-reversion pressure against speculators (1).
  • Conditional Invalidation: Spec_zscore falling significantly below -2.0, triggering a confirmed high tail-risk regime.
  • Stability is volatile; the signal recently touched an extreme short state (-2.05) before slightly retracing to current levels.

Scenario Balance:

  • Dominant base case: Persistence of downward price pressure driven by the restrictive monetary policy consensus.
  • Most plausible upside risk: A tactical short squeeze triggered by speculative de-risking if price stabilizes.
  • Most plausible downside risk: Trend acceleration if speculative selling breaches multi-year extremes.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Tactical (weeks): CoT data reflects positioning shifts that typically precede short-term price adjustments (1).
  • Aggregation Weight: Medium; the proximity to extreme thresholds warrants attention, but the lack of a current "Extreme" flag suggests caution.

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs Federal Reserve policy expectations and fixed-income liquidity.
  • Implies a restrictive monetary policy bias through rising speculative short conviction (1).
  • Cycle position: not determined.
  • Interacts with inflation and labor data to confirm or invalidate the "Higher for Longer" policy narrative (1).

Regime Context:

  • The regime is persistent in its short bias but transitioned from an "Elevated Risk" state to "High Tension" as z-scores marginally improved.
  • Direction of change: Stabilising at extreme tension levels.

Model Limitations:

  • Weekly reporting lag may obscure real-time positioning shifts following major data releases (1).
  • Extremes can persist for extended periods during strong structural trends (1).

Data & References:

  • SOFR-3M CoT Analysis (latest observation: 2026-05-12) (1).
  • Speculative Net %OI (-8.6) and Tension Score (3.91) are the primary drivers.
  • Public datasets: US CPI Inflation Trends and FOMC Meeting Minutes would improve interpretation.
SOF 5Y - Individual Market Analysis

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given Spec_Net_%OI of 20.0%, a Spec_zscore of 0.77, and positive 4-week flow momentum (+3.6), this setup aligns with Upward-biased price paths and Normal volatility, where the dominant risk is Trend continuation, not Mean reversion.
  • The signal currently identifies a "Balanced_Long_Bias" regime, reflecting a shift toward disinflationary or easing expectations (1).
  • Conviction Band: Medium; Interpretation Confidence: High Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Improving; Threshold Proximity: Far; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • Spec_zscore < 2 indicates a "healthy" trend-following regime rather than speculative exhaustion (1).
  • Positive Flow Momentum aligning with Net Position direction implies increasing sponsorship for the current price path (1).
  • Positioning Tension Score (1.54) measures stability in the medium-term policy transmission narrative (1).
  • 5 YEAR ERIS SOFR SWAP (Observation: 2026-05-12).

Key Dynamics:

  • Dominant drivers include the transition to a 20.0% Speculator Net Long position and a recent surge in "Long_Build" flow (1).
  • Momentum has shifted from a short-biased structure in April to a consistent long-biased build in May (1).
  • No internal tensions; speculators and flow direction are currently synchronized.
  • Conditional Invalidation: A multi-week flow reversal that opposes the net position direction.
  • Signal stability is improving as recent weekly observations show persistent long-side accumulation.

Scenario Balance:

  • Base Case dominant: Consolidation of easing expectations supports a persistent upward bias in bond-equivalent pricing.
  • Upside Risk: Accelerated long-loading triggered by growth data undershooting neutral-rate assumptions.
  • Downside Risk: Reflationary shocks forcing a "Long_Reduction" squeeze if the higher-for-longer narrative returns.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months). This reflects shifts in medium-term macro beliefs and neutral-rate assumptions (1).
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Medium. The trend is healthy and sponsored, but lacks the high-conviction extremes found in exhaustion regimes.

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs the multi-year growth-inflation balance and strategic investor policy expectations (1).
  • Economic mechanism: Implied easing in medium-term policy transmission.
  • Cycle position: Not determined.
  • Typically interacts with front-end SOFR and yield curve slope signals to confirm regime transitions.

Regime Context:

  • The signal recently entered the "Balanced_Long_Bias" regime in May after a 10-week period of "Balanced_Short_Bias" (1).
  • Direction of change: Strengthening, as evidenced by rising speculators' net contracts reaching 37,363 (1).

Model Limitations:

  • Subject to weekly CoT reporting lags and requires sustained narrative shifts for mean-reversion signals (1).

Data & References:

  • CFTC Legacy Report (5 YEAR ERIS SOFR SWAP), latest date: 2026-05-12 (1).
  • Influential datapoints: Speculator Net %OI (20.0%) and Flow_4w (3.6).
  • Additional data: U.S. 5Y Treasury yields and PCE inflation prints would improve regime depth.
